comment.body: Approve a focused Mouse Without Borders design pass for Issue 50116.

Thanks for documenting the manual settings.json workaround — that is the key clue here, because it shows the file format can work when both machines end up with the same persisted key. Please provide:

1. Fresh PowerToys diagnostic ZIP files from both machines captured immediately after a failed setup attempt: reproduce the KeysNotMatched problem and then add /bugreport comments from both machines right away, attaching both generated ZIP files.
2. The install source/scope for each machine (WinGet, Store, or GitHub; user vs system) and whether either PowerToys instance was running elevated during setup.

That will confirm whether the bug is purely in the shared SecurityKey save/reload path or whether the two machines are editing different settings locations.

proposed_fixes.title: Serialize MWB security-key updates before reopening sockets
proposed_fixes.root_cause: MWB appears to accept a new key through one UI path and then reread or overwrite it through another settings save/watch path before both peers share the same stable value.
plan: Route SecurityKey changes through one normalized persistence method.
Debounce self-triggered watcher updates before reopening sockets.
Keep saved key, Encryption.MyKey, and reopened sockets in sync across both settings surfaces.
verification: Change the key from each supported settings surface and verify both machines reconnect without manual JSON edits.
Confirm the saved SecurityKey remains identical after closing and reopening MWB and Settings.

confidence.rationale: Workaround strongly points at the save/reload path, but paired diagnostics would still raise confidence.
